I've written the scene at `drafts/r047-google-indexed-every-service-page-except/scene.html`. The automatic check says **PASS**, and I looked at stills across the whole reel at phone size. The reel runs about 30.7 seconds: 27.6 seconds of speech, Maya's look to camera, then the end card.

It follows the template's shape. It loads `lines.js` as it is, uses the story's pauses for the timing, creates Floey first and then Maya with `floey: F`, has each line spoken by its own speaker, drives everything from one paused timeline, and sets the same `window.*` values as the template.

**How it plays:**
- **Hook:** frame one already shows the problem. The client's message "Why isn't Hove on Google?" is on screen. Maya clicks the trackpad three times, 0.45 seconds apart, while Floey blinks slowly at her. The message slides away and we push into her panic, with a jolt on "Google". On "I've begged" the Search Console Pages report swings in. Three towns show Indexed, and Hove is the one ringed red row, with Search Console's full wording "Duplicate without user-selected canonical" kept in full on two lines.
- **Floey's reframe:** Floey alone on the laptop, deadpan, with one chip and a tilt toward the screen. On "It picked Brighton" the URL Inspection screen comes in and the ring lands on Google's chosen page, `/brighton-oven-cleaning`. It stays up through Maya's "Duplicate?", so the word she reacts to is on screen.
- **Doubt and tip:** in the wide shot Maya crosses her arms, offended, and Floey gives a slow head tilt. For the tip Floey looks from the screen to Maya and back, then preens. Maya moves to chin-in-hand, then types to open the two pages side by side.
- **Check:** the "Brighton vs Hove" table. Rows land in time with her full stops. The intro row gets the ring and a ding on "Same intro".
- **Payoff:** a close-up of Maya: surprised on "Oh.", sad on "swapped the town", with her eyes sliding guiltily to Floey. Then Floey: a slow blink on "Twins" and one tongue flick instead of a second preen.
- **Fix:** Hove's intro rewrites to "From Church Road to the seafront" while she types. The review is **pasted** (one click, no typing sound), so she isn't seen writing a fake review. The finished table stays up about 1.7 seconds after the last change.
- **Button:** "Why, Google?" said flat to the ceiling. Floey turns to camera, answers for Google, and winks. Then Maya gives the lens a long look for about 2.4 seconds before the end card.

**Where I went against the brief, and why:**
- **Extra row on the URL Inspection screen:** I added a "Page indexing: Duplicate without user-selected canonical" row. Real URL Inspection shows this status, and it gives Maya's "Duplicate?" something to read.
- **Table text drawn by the scene:** `DUO.listInsert` still draws the card, the ring and the row slide, but it can't wrap text, and the long cells would have overlapped. So the scene measures every cell and wraps it to two lines when needed, never shortening it.
- **Faces:** the brief asks for faces Maya doesn't have ("sheepish", "determined"). I used her real ones instead: annoyed while she fixes the page, then proud, and deadpan for "Why, Google?".

**Still open, because the lines are fixed:** the editor notes that need different lines are not addressed. These are naming "Request Indexing" in the hook, moving "Why, Google?" to before the fix, and making line 8 sound less like a to-do list. Voice emotions are also set by the lines, so "Why, Google?" is still marked determined and may sound rallying rather than flat.
